A parameterization of flat Gaussians as triangle faces.
It sets one scaling axis to $\epsilon$, allowing Gaussians to be represented as 2D triangles in 3D space.
It is chosen when stable, triangle-based physics simulation is required for Gaussian splats. [Link](6003-games.md)
A particle-based physics simulation method used in GASP to compute vertex trajectories.

It is chosen for its ability to handle large deformations and complex material behaviors (cloth, sand, etc.) as a black-box engine. [Link](../../volume-rendering/differentiable-and-inverse-volume-rendering/radiance-field-optimization/3d-gaussian-splatting/mpm.md)
A method that adapts Newtonian dynamics to 3D Gaussians using first-order approximation of deformation maps.
GASP differs by using GaMeS triangles and black-box physics, avoiding the need for engine modifications or linear approximations. [Link](6002-physgaussian.md)
*   **Time Complexity:** The conversion to triangles and back is linear with respect to the number of Gaussians $p$.
The physics simulation cost depends on the engine (e.g., MPM complexity).
*   **When to use:** When simulating deformable objects (cloth, jelly, sand) with Gaussian Splatting and you want to leverage existing physics engines without modifying them.
*   **When not to use:** When high-fidelity continuous deformation fields are required beyond the triangle approximation, or when the physics engine cannot handle point clouds efficiently.
